land.text: Timur's imperial capital Samarqand and Tashkent, where Khalil Sultan 'proclaimed himself emperor' soon after Timur's death in February 1405

predecessors.note: Khalil Sultan seized Transoxiana from the Timurid Empire (Timur) at his grandfather's death; Shah Rukh at Herat was the other claimant.

land.text: Samarkand and Transoxiana, taken back by Shah Rukh in May 1409 and, after the 1449-1451 rivals, by Abu Sa'id Mirza in June 1451

successors.note: The land returns to the Timurid Empire twice: Shah Rukh (13 May 1409), then Abu Sa'id Mirza who 'defeated Abdullah Mirza ... and executed him in 1451'. Between 1410 and 1448 the dossier holds no land (Ulugh Beg governs Transoxiana for Shah Rukh).

capitals.name: Samarkand
capitals.note: Khalil Sultan 'seized the royal treasury, as well as Timur's imperial capital Samarqand'; he had been proclaimed at Tashkent. Coordinates are those of Samarkand, approximate; no page gives them.

capitals.name: Samarkand
capitals.note: Abdal-Latif and Abdullah Mirza are listed 'Timurid Empire (in Samarkand)' (Abdullah Mirza page succession box); Abdullah is 'Amir of the Timurid Empire in Transoxiana'.

rulers.name: Khalil Sultan
rulers.note: 'the Timurid ruler of Transoxiana from 18 February 1405 to 1409'; Shah Rukh entered Samarkand unopposed on 13 May 1409; Khalil then governed Ray and died in 1411.

rulers.name: Abdal-Latif Mirza
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign: 27 October 1449 - 9 May 1450'; killed at Samarkand.

rulers.name: Abdullah Mirza
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign: 9 May 1450 - June 1451'; defeated and executed by Abu Sa'id Mirza in 1451.

correction.text: Khalil Sultan, 'the Timurid ruler of Transoxiana from 18 February 1405 to 1409', with Tashkent where he was proclaimed, Samarkand which he seized and the Ferghana Valley he had been given in 1402

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria shape: Cliopatria draws Transoxiana as Timurid Empire all through 1405-1409, shapes 1402 and 1407). The Khalil Sultan page gives the title 'ruler of Transoxiana' and 'in 1402 was given rule of the Ferghana Valley', no boundary and no area; the Timurid page's 1405 estimate of 4.4 M km2 is for the whole empire. The Transoxiana region is the researcher's reading.

correction.text: Abdal-Latif Mirza (reign 27 October 1449 - 9 May 1450) and Abdullah Mirza (9 May 1450 - June 1451), 'Amir of the Timurid Empire in Transoxiana', 'in Samarkand'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria keeps Transoxiana in the Timurid shape 1440-1449 and 1450-1452). The pages give Samarkand and 'Transoxiana', no boundary: Abu Sa'id Mirza marched on Samarkand from Tashkent in 1451, so Tashkent was probably already outside the rivals' hands; the region is generous to the rivals there.

region.text: Tashkent, where Khalil Sultan 'proclaimed himself emperor', and Samarqand, Timur's capital, which he seized

ledger.note: 18 February 1405: Khalil Sultan takes Timur's throne in Transoxiana. 'Khalil Sultan was the Timurid ruler of Transoxiana from 18 February 1405 to 1409'; the Shah Rukh page: he 'proclaimed himself emperor at Tashkent soon after his grandfather's death' and 'seized the royal treasury, as well as Timur's imperial capital Samarqand' (no month for the seizure). The cities are the pages'; the radii are the researcher's.

region.text: Transoxiana, 'the Timurid ruler of Transoxiana from 18 February 1405 to 1409'

ledger.note: 1405: Khalil Sultan holds Transoxiana against Shah Rukh at Herat, who 'marched his army out of Herat to the Oxus river but made no offensive move against his nephew at this point' (Shah Rukh page). The Timurid Empire dossier books the same land as a loss to 'Khalil Sultan (rival Timurid emperor)'.

region.text: Samarkand and Transoxiana, entered by Shah Rukh unopposed

ledger.note: 13 May 1409: Shah Rukh enters Samarkand unopposed and ends Khalil Sultan's rule. Khalil Sultan page: Shah Rukh 'entered the city unopposed on May 13, 1409'; the Shah Rukh page: 'It was not until 1409 that the war started to turn in Shah Rukh's favour', 'Samarqand, having been left abandoned, was taken unopposed by Shah Rukh'. Khalil was then appointed governor of Ray and 'died there in 1411'. The dossier holds no land from 1410 to 1448.

region.text: Samarkand and Transoxiana, taken by Abdal-Latif Mirza from his father Ulugh Beg

ledger.note: October 1449: Abdal-Latif Mirza overthrows and has his father Ulugh Beg killed, and rules Samarkand. 'He defeated his father at Dimashq, near Samarkand, in the fall of 1449'; infobox 'Reign: 27 October 1449 - 9 May 1450'. The Shah Rukh page has Ulugh Beg 'murdered by his son Abdal-Latif in 1449'. The Timurid Empire dossier books the same land as a loss to 'Abdal-Latif Mirza (Timurid rival)'.

9 May 1450: Abdal-Latif is killed at Samarkand and his cousin Abdullah Mirza, whom he had imprisoned, becomes ruler of Samarkand (Abdullah Mirza page: 'Reign: 9 May 1450 - June 1451'; Abdal-Latif page: 'He was succeeded by his cousin Abdullah Mirza', 'Died: 9 May 1450'). No land changes hands.

region.text: Samarkand and Transoxiana, taken by Abu Sa'id Mirza

ledger.note: June 1451: Abu Sa'id Mirza takes Samarkand and executes Abdullah Mirza. 'Marching from Tashkent to Samarkand with the support of Abu'l-Khayr Khan, Abu Sa'id Mirza defeated Abdullah Mirza ... and executed him in 1451, taking his place on the throne'; infobox 'Died: June 1451'. The Timurid Empire page: 'Abu Sa'id Mirza (r. 1451-1469) briefly reunited most of the empire'.

wars.name: Timurid war of succession of 1405-1409 (Shah Rukh against Khalil Sultan)
wars.outcome: After 'a series of unproductive negotiations as well as many military encounters' the war 'started to turn in Shah Rukh's favour' in 1409; Samarkand 'was taken unopposed by Shah Rukh' on 13 May 1409.
wars.note: The pages give no battle that took or held ground before 1409, so no contest is recorded and the zones are empty; Khalil's years are drawn as his Transoxiana against Shah Rukh's empire.

wars.name: Timurid civil war of 1447-1451 (Ulugh Beg, Abdal-Latif, Abdullah Mirza, Abu Sa'id Mirza)
wars.outcome: Abdal-Latif's 1449 revolt killed Ulugh Beg and led to 'civil war'; Abdullah Mirza held Samarkand from May 1450 until Abu Sa'id Mirza defeated and executed him in June 1451.
wars.note: Timurid Empire page: 'his execution in 1449 after a revolt by his son Abdal-Latif Mirza' plunged the empire into civil war; Abu Sa'id Mirza 'briefly reunited most of the empire'. Ulugh Beg's own 1447-1449 rule of Samarkand is in the timurid-empire dossier. Zones are empty because single battles decided the land at once: Abdal-Latif 'defeated his father at Dimashq, near Samarkand, in the fall of 1449' (Abdal-Latif Mirza page) and Abu Sa'id 'defeated Abdullah Mirza and executed him in 1451' (Abdullah Mirza page); the ledger's October 1449 gain and June 1451 dissolve carry the change, and no contest is drawn (n-mid review).

certainty.note: The Khalil Sultan page names a title (ruler of Transoxiana) and cities, never a boundary.
The dossier holds no land in these years (Transoxiana is the Timurid Empire's, under Ulugh Beg as governor); the entry only keeps certainty continuous.
Samarkand is certain; the extent of the rivals' Transoxiana is not given by any page.

sources.title: Abdal-Latif Mirza

sources.title: Abdullah Mirza

sources.title: Timurid Empire

notes: Requested by the p1400-p1499 window (Timurid ledger L17 and L34 give Samarkand and Tashkent to counterparts without dossiers). The dossier covers two episodes of rival Timurid rule at Samarkand with one slug, as the brief asks: Khalil Sultan 1405-1409, and Abdal-Latif Mirza then Abdullah Mirza 1449-1451. Between them (1410-1448) the dossier holds no land: the loss of 13 May 1409 returns Transoxiana to the Timurid Empire and the gain of October 1449 takes it again; if the compiler needs a continuous life, split the dossier into khalil-sultan (1405-1409) and abdal-latif-and-abdullah-mirza (1449-1451). Existing counterpart strings to update (not edited here): the timurid-empire ledger names 'Khalil Sultan (rival Timurid emperor)' (1405 loss, 1409 gain), 'Abdal-Latif Mirza (Timurid rival)' (1449 loss) and 'Abdullah Mirza (Timurid rival)' (1451 gain); all four should read khalil-sultan-and-rival-timurids. Cliopatria draws Transoxiana as Timurid in both episodes, so the compiler must let these ledger events cut it out. Not settled: how much of Transoxiana the rivals held (the pages say 'Transoxiana' and 'Samarkand'; Abu Sa'id marched from Tashkent in 1451); whether Khalil held Ferghana to 1409 (given 1402); Abdal-Latif's Balkh governorship and brief hold of Herat after Babur Mirza (end of 1448, Abdal-Latif page) are not in the ledger. Shah Malik, Khudaidad and Muhammad Jahangir (the khan Khalil installed, aged nine) are not on the pages as territorial actors. Wikidata ids not known. The 1405 month is Khalil's reign start (18 February) per the Khalil Sultan page; the Timurid Empire dossier has Timur's death 17/18 February.
